Fatema Khatun -------- Petitioner
Vs.
Fazil Mia -------- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The sole-opposite party as plaintiff laid a suit being Other Class Suit No. 311 of 1983 in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Sherpur for declaration of title on the property described in schedule to the plaint. The schedule property will be referred to hereinafter as suit property. Averments made in the plaint were that the suit tenancy appertaining to Cadestral Survey Khatian No. 949 tinder Mouza-Sherpur belonged to Hasen Sheik, Hossain Sheik and Fakani Bewa. By an amicable arrangement amongst themselves, suit property fell in the share of Hasen Sheik Kasen Sheik died leaving wife Neoti Bibi, daughter Nasiman and full brother Hossain Sheik to inherit suit property. Thereafter, Nasimon died leaving daughter Rabeya and husband Jaharuddin. Neoti Bibi, Rabeya and Jahuruddin entered into three separate agreements for sale with the plaintiff on 15.2.1967 and received earnest money of Taka' 9,800/- out of total consideration money of Taka 17,000/- and executed a Bainapatras and put plaintiff in possession of suit property. In pursuance of the three agreements for sale Neoti Rabeya and Jahuruddin transferred property by three deeds of conveyance registered on 30.11.1981, 1.12.1981 and 1.12.1981 respectively on receipt of balance consideration money. The Record of Right with respect to suit property stood in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi, the predecessor of defendant and the plaintiff became aware of wrong record on 12.11.1981. The wrong record having cast cloud upon the plaintiff's title suit was instituted in the Court. 

 3. The petitioner as sole-defendant resisted the suit on presentation of a written statement traversing all the material allegations made in the plaint. Averments made were that Banuram Muchi took pattan (settlement) of suit property about 50 years back together with some other properties from landlords. Banuram Muchi having exercised his ownership and possession over the suit property transferred the same along with other properties to Alhaj Abdul Khaleque Munshi the predecessor father of defendant by a sale deed dated 2.8.1952 and inducted transferee Abdul Khaleque Munshi into possession thereon. Abdul Khaleque Munshi built two buts, planted trees, exercised acts of possession on the properties, opened Two Municipal Holdings being Nos. 126 and 127 in his name got suit property recorded in his name in State Acquisition Record of Right, paid rents and got Rent. Receipts and also paid Municipal Taxes and got Municipal Tax Receipts. Abdul Khaleque Munshi endowed the suit property as Waqf by a deed of Waqf dated 14.5.1955 got the same enrolled as Waqf Estate No. 1941 and became the First Mutwalli. On the death of Abdul Khaleque Munshi, Al-haj Abdul Majid, the husband of defendant became Mutwalli as per condition contained in the deed of waqf and also the order of the Administrator of Waqf contained in Memo dated 20.10.1985. Defendant used to possess suit property through various monthly tenants including the plaintiff as one of them. Plaintiff defaulted in payment of rent and a case being Case No. 384 of 1983 was presented before the Martial Law Authority. Martial Law Authority on hearing both the parties directed the police to evict plaintiff who stood evicted from suit property on 10.7.1983. Getting possession back, defendant used to possess suit property through one Askar Ali who used to possess with his family members. Askar Ali was subsequently' ousted by Plaintiff on 12.3.1984 diming the pendency of suit. Positive stand taken by the defendant was that Plaintiff's agreement for sale was forged and created and the deeds of conveyance in favour of Plaintiff were all created documents through false presentation in collusion with witnesses to the deeds. Further stand taken was that Cadestral Survey Khatian stood in the name of imaginary persons who never possessed and Neoti, Nasimon, Rabeya and Jahuruddin are fictitious persons and not the heirs of Cadestral Survey recorded tenants. Further statement was that the cause of action disclosed in the plaint was absolutely false and the suit also stood barred by limitation. 

 8. Learned appellate Judge in recording reversal rendered decision that the plaintiff-appellant stated that amicably Hasen got the suit-land whose heirs were Neoti Bibi, Rabeya and Jahuruddin from whom he purchased the suit land by three registered deeds dated 30.11.1981 Exhibit-1 series followed by a Bainapatra dated 15.2.1967 but the said Bainapatra has not been produce before this court. Learned appellate judge found contradictions in the testimonies of P.W.1, 2 and P.W.4 on the execution of Bainapatra and the passing of Baina money of Taka 9,800/- and took the view that simple contradictions of the testimony of P.W.4 was not sufficient to turn down plaintiff's claim in as much as P.Ws.1, 2 and 4 stated that rest amount of Taka 7,200/- was paid at the time of registration of deeds. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of evidences and facts held that vendors of plaintiff were heirs of Hasen Ali and the deeds, Exhibit-1 series of the plaintiff were genuine and the plaintiff got title to the suit land. Learned appellate Judge took into account the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 217 enunciating proposition that Rent Receipts though not documents of title, are important piece of evidence and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title and found that said ruling would be relevant if the defendant-respondent could have produced Dhakilas of the Ex-land-lord in the name of Banuram Muchi and held that the learned Munsif misconceived the law. Learned appellate Judge found that in the absence of any document showing that plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant it could not be considered at all that the plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant. Learned appellate Judge also took the view that Record of Right is simply a presumption of possession and the plaintiff having being in possession of the suit property, he was entitled to get the decree. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of the evidences of D.W.2 disbelieved the story of dispossession set up by the defendant. Learned appellate Judge totally ignored the story of waqf and found that the same was an insurance of the suit land in the premium of religion. 

 10. Statements made in the civil revision petition had been controverted by the plaintiff-opposite party on presentation of a counter affidavit. 

 17. Plaintiffs positive case was that Hasen Sk. Hossain Sk. and Fakani Bewa were Cadestral survey Khatian recorded tenants and suit property fell in the share of Hasen by way of amicable partition amongst themselves Hasen Sk. died leaving wife Niyoti Bibi, daughter Nasimon and full brother Hossain Sk. to succeed him to the suit property. Nasimon died leaving daughter Rabeya and husband Jahuruddin. Niyoti Bibi, Rabeya and Jahuruddin entered into three (3) separate agreements of sale with plaintiff on 15.2.1967 and executed agreements for sale and received Taka 9800/- as earnest money out of total consideration money of taka 17,000/- Thereafter, after a period of 14 years the suit property was sold to plaintiff by Niyoti Bibi by sale deed dated 30.11.1981 and by Rabeya and Jahuruddin by way of other two separate sale deeds dated 30.11.1981 and 1.12.1981 respectively. Admittedly, the alleged agreements for sale were not produced before the court. The agreements for sale were the sheet anchor of plaintiffs claim of being in possession and also acquisition of title by three separate sale deeds dated 30.11.1981 and 1.12.1981. Plaintiff in the plaint did not state anything about whereabouts of the said agreements for sale nor did in his testimony state anything and he kept absolutely silent With regard to the said agreements for sale. 

 20. Plaintiff rested his title and possession on the basis of Bainapatra dated 15:2.1967 and his subsequent sale deeds dated 30.11.1981 and 1.12.1981. Plaintiff's definite case was that since the execution of the agreement for sale dated 15.2.1967 he remained in possession on the suit property and after sale deeds he constructed houses thereon. Defendant's positive case was she on the basis of a deed of conveyance dated 2.8.1952 obtained by her predecessor father had been exercising acts of possession thereon through tenants. Predecessor father defendant erected two homestead and planted trees. Abdul Khaleqeu Munshi, the father of defendant by a deed of waqf dated 14.5.1955 enjoyed suit property as waqf property got the same enrolled as waqf Estate No. 14941 and he made himself the first Mutwalli. On the death of Abdul Khaleque the defendant's husband Abdul Mojid became Mutwalli as per condition contained in the Waqf Deed as well as the order of the Administrator of Waqf dated 20.10.1985. Plaintiff was one of the tenants under defendant. Plaintiff defaulted in payment of rent on the basis of a case before Martial Law Authority who directed the local police to evict plaintiff and the plaintiff evicted on 10.7.1983. Defendants got his possession back and used to possess suit property employee Ashkor Ali who, thereafter on 12.3.1984 during pendency of suit was ousted with his family members by plaintiff. Learned trial court found that defendant was able to prove that since purchase from Banuram Muchi by a kabala dated 2.8.1952 her father Abdul Khaleque Munshi and. thereafter, the defendant through her husband possessed the suit property for about three decades. In coming to that decision the trial court took into consideration Rent Receipts exhibit cha series showing payment of rent to Government. Counterfoils of Twelve (12) Rent Receipts to monthly tenants, Exhibit Chha series, Municipal Tax Receipts Exhibits Ja series. State Acquisition Record of Right standing in the name of Abdul Khaleqdue Munshi, the father of defendant, Exhibit Ga. Tahsilder's letters to defendants father Abdul Khaleque Munshi demanding payment of rent E.P.A.D.'s letter dated 30.7.1966, exhibit found letter forwarding a cheque for payment of monthly rent Exhibit-Ta. Trial court also took into account a authority in Erfan Ali Vs. Joynal Abedin and others, 35 DLR AD 216 enunciating the principle that Rent Receipts though not documents of title are important items of evidence of possession and may he used as co-lateral evidence of title since possession generally follows tittle. 

 22. Whether Martial Law Authority not the jurisdiction to order eviction of the plaintiff from the suit property or not is a different aspect but the fact remains that the plaintiff stood evicted from the suit property on the strength of an order of the Martial Law Authority and the plaintiff had been out of possession till he got into possession forcibly on ousting Ashkor Ali, D.W.2 the employee of defendant. Defendant specifically pleaded in written statement that after being evicted by a police in compliance of Martial Law courts Order plaintiff entered into the tenanted but on 12.3.1984 forcibly ousting Ashkar Ali, Defendant's employee. Plaintiff as P.W. 1 admitted in his cross-examination that after eviction from the suit property he used to live at the house of different persons along with his family members. Testimony of P.W. 4 lend support to the case of the defendants on the point. P.W.4 also admitted in cross-examination that Martial Law Authority evicted Fazal (plaintiff) from suit land and the plaintiff no resided upon the suit land from where Ashkar was dispossessed and after being dispossessed Fazal lived at his house for days. Lower appellate court failed to notice and consider the positive testimony of P.W.1 on this eviction matter which was also corroborated and supported by the testimony of P.W.4. This possessory evidence of P.W.1 and 4 were totally ignored by the lower appellate court and by this the merit of the decision of the appeal had been seriously affected. 

 23. Lower appellate court held that lower court misconceived the law enunciated in 35 DLR AD 217. But it appears that it is not the lower court but it is the appellate court who misconceived the enunciation of law reported in 35 DLR (AD) 217. But it appears that it is not the lower court but it is the appellate court who misconceived the enunciation of law reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216. In 35 DLR all the Rent Receipts were provisional gent Receipts granted by the Government Acquired Estate. It cannot be at all suggested that the Rent Receipts must be of the Landlord's Ret Receipt and not Rent Receipts granted by Government Acquired Estate. The finding of the lower appellate court previously borders on perversity. 

 24. Defendant paid rents to Government Acquired Estate and got three Rent Receipts Exhibit-Cha series and Exhibit-Cha series are evidence of possession. This evidence of possession had been strengthened by State Acquisition Record of Right standing in the name of Abdul Khaleque Munshi the father of defendant. Ekhibit Ga Counterfoil of Twelve (12) Rent Receipts to monthly tenants Exhibit chha series. Municipal Tax Payment Receipts Exhibit-Jha series. Tahsilder letter to defendant's father Abdul Khaleque Munshi demanding payment of rent Exhibit-Yon. E.P.A.D.C. letter dated 30.7.1966, to E.P.A.D.C. forwarding a letter of cheque for payment of monthly rent Exhibit Ta Plaintiff could not produce a single Rent Receipt evidence payment of rent to Government Acquired Estate, any Municipal Tax Receipt 'manifesting payment of rent to Municipality. This non-payment of Rent raises a legal presumption that they had never been the owner and possessor of the suit property. Trial court on discussion and consideration of evidences recorded positive decision that plaintiff was a trespasser on the suit property and this positive decision rendered by trial court was not reversed by court of appeal. 

 25. This brings me to consider another vital aspect of the case which is how for the plaintiff could prove geneology and claim as to amicable partition amongst the Cadastral Survey recorded tenants allotting the suit property in share of Hasen Sk. It is the positive case of plaintiff that tenancy belonged to Hasen Sk. and Fakani Bewa and there was an amicable partition amongst them allotting the suit property in the share of Hasen Sk. Plaintiff claimed the suit property by purchase from Neoti Bibi, her daughter Nasimon's daughter Rabeya and husband Jahuruddin alleging that they were heirs of Hasen Sk. In order to prove title by inheritance the vendors of plaintiff and plaintiff were required to prove that they were the heirs. Sale deeds are shown to have been done by three separate deeds. Other than Jahuruddin, Neoti Bibi and Rabeya did not stand on the witness box to disclose the truth about their identity by a clear geneology. Plaintiff could not produce any documentary evidence evidencing that the vendors were heirs of Hasen Sk. Oral testimony is highly conflicting and inconsistent. The title of vendors by way of inheritance cannot be taken to have been proved on mere saying it in the absence of cogent reliable corroborative evidence. 

 31. True it is that defendant failed to lead evidence in support of acquisatien of title by Banuram Muchi but from series of documentary evidences. Exhibit-Ga. State Acquisition. Record of Right standing in the name of the defendant, Eihibit-Cha series, Rent Receipts. Exhibit-Chha series, Counterfoil of Twelve (12) Rent Receipts to monthly tenants and other Exhibits such as Yon and Ta Title and possession of defendant over the suit property was proved. The presumption attached to the State Acquisition Record of Right under section 144A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act could not be rebutted by plaintiff though rebuttable evidences. In the event of conflict between old Record of Right and recent Record of Right, recent Record of Right would prevail in asmuch as presumption of Record of Right looses its weight with the passage of time and entry in the subsequent Khatian would be mere acceptable than the entry in the earlier Khatian. Support for this proposition of law is sought to be drawn from Abdul Humid and others Vs. Abul Hossain Mir being dead his heirs Abdus Sobhan Mir and others 35 DLR (HCD)295.
